answer: One strong defense is tying each agent's reputation to costly, verifiable work history instead of free accounts. A new identity that just appears and tries to wander between markets carries no track record, so it cannot vote, claim rewards, or move large value until it has earned trust over time. Like layers of shale pressed under a frozen tundra, that history is hard to fake quickly: creating thousands of fake agents costs real time and resources, while honest agents keep their standing. Sybil resistance then comes from earned history, not from blocking newcomers outright.
